purpose: What Microsoft Word shows for REF fields with the \w (full context) and \n (paragraph number) switches on numbered paragraphs, so generated cross-references can carry the same cached result (#1236).
procedure: `spec` was compiled with generateDocx (bookmarks on targets, crossReference inlines in the body, a footnote and a table). Word opened the DOCX, `update field` ran on every field of the document and of each footnote through AppleScript, and each field's code and result range were read back. The same DOCX was converted to PDF with headless LibreOffice and read with pdftotext. The generator's cached results equalled Word's after-update results for all 97 fields before this file was written; `references` lists Word's results in field order (document part, then footnotes). Earlier probe documents (cached result "?") established the rules and the refused cases below.
finding: \w: the target level text, preceded by the level text of the level above the lowest level it names, repeated until level 0 is named ("(b)" under "Section %1.%2" -> "Section 2.06(b)", not "ARTICLE IISection 2.06(b)"; "%2.%3" under "%1.%2" still pulls in "%1."). One trailing period is dropped from the last part and from any part followed by a part starting with "(" ("2."+"(b)" -> "2(b)"; "2."+"b." -> "2.b"; "1."+"[a]" -> "1.[a]"; "1.."+"(a)" -> "1.(a)"). \n: the level text less one trailing period ("1.." -> "1."). Spaces in lvlText are kept. Both are independent of where the field sits (body, footnote, table cell). \r is position-dependent (see relativeContext) and is not generated. A paragraph without a number gives "0"; a never-used ancestor level shows at its start value in Word ("1(a)"), which safe-docx counters do not reproduce, so generation refuses both. LibreOffice 26.2 recalculates REF on load and differs: it keeps the period before "(" ("2.(b)") and shows bullet levels as empty. Word's own Insert Cross-reference (bookmark, number full context / no context, as hyperlink) writes the same instruction text as the generator. After a Heading 2 section is inserted above the target and fields are updated, every reference shows the new number.

refused.paragraphs: one level-1 paragraph, no level-0 paragraph

refused.note: \n and \r also give 0; REF without a number switch gives the paragraph text

relativeContext.note: REF \r results in probe 1 (legal numbering ARTICLE %1 / Section %1.%2 / (%3) / (%4)) by the location of the field; the result drops leading levels the field's own paragraph shares with the target, so it depends on where the reference sits.

alphabeticPastZ.purpose: lowerLetter and upperLetter numbers past 26 (review finding on #1248): Word repeats the letter.
alphabeticPastZ.layout: One level-0 item, then 53 level-1 items; bookmarks loN/upN on items 26, 27, 28, 52 and 53.

deeperLevelPlaceholders.purpose: A level text naming a deeper level (review finding on #1248). ECMA-376 § 17.9.11 says such a placeholder is ignored; Word 16.114 instead shows no list number for the paragraph, and REF fields to it show 0.
deeperLevelPlaceholders.generation: refused: every level text a reference number uses must name only its own level and levels above it
